headline: Huang agrees to testify to US Congress before leaving Nvidia
dek: The closed-door hearing is due before Thanksgiving, per Engadget.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The deal
body: Jensen Huang agreed to testify to US Congress in a closed hearing, hours before resigning, per Engadget.
He agreed after lawmakers threatened a subpoena (Engadget).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Mast's remarks
body: Republican Brian Mast said he does not want to hurt Nvidia, but Huang has serious questions to answer (Engadget).
He expects the session to be filmed and transcribed, per Bloomberg cited by Engadget.

items.t: Democrats may seek an open session (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: Jensen Huang agreed to testify to Congress, hours before leaving Nvidia's helm.
body: Per Engadget, he accepted the closed-door hearing after being threatened with a subpoena. Republican Brian Mast said the session should take place before Thanksgiving. It will bring together the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, per Engadget.

TechCrunch says the focus is the security implications of the case and that it is unclear whether Democrats will also summon him to a public session. Per Bloomberg cited by Engadget, the committee chair expects the hearing to be filmed and transcribed, which could make its content public later.
